sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Transformers is Hugging Face's Python library that defines hundreds of pretrained AI models for text, images, audio and video. You can load a model from the Hugging Face Hub and use it for inference or training in a few lines.
sixtySeconds.problem: Every new model architecture would otherwise need its own code. Transformers writes each model once, in PyTorch, in a standard structure, and other tools such as vLLM, Unsloth, SGLang and llama.cpp build on those definitions.
whoFor: ML engineers fine-tuning language or vision models
Builders of inference and training tools
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it when you want the widest selection of open models with one consistent API. For high-throughput serving in production, the README points to inference engines like vLLM that use Transformers models as a backend.
requirements: A GPU helps for larger models

overview: Transformers is the model-definition framework for text, vision, audio, video and multimodal models. Each model is one file that reads top to bottom, and new architectures are added as they are released and matched to their original results.

The Pipeline class is the quickest way in: it preprocesses input, runs the model and postprocesses output for a task. You can also generate text with LLMs and vision-language models, chat in the terminal with transformers chat, and serve a model over HTTP with transformers serve for experiments and moderate load.

The library is designed to be easy for people and coding agents to read and change. You can register your own attention function or load optimized kernels from the Hub without editing model code. The README includes a prompt to help coding agents use the current v5 APIs.

tutorial.title: Ask a chat model a question with a pipeline
tutorial.useCase: Load a small chat model from the Hub and get an answer in Python.

steps.title: Create a pipeline and send a message
steps.code:
from transformers import pipeline

pipe = pipeline(task="text-generation", model="Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B")
messages = [
    {"role": "user", "content": "What's the secret to baking a really good cake? Answer in one sentence."},
]
output = pipe(messages, tokenizer_encode_kwargs={"enable_thinking": False})
print(output[0]["generated_text"][-1]["content"])

tutorial.expected: The model downloads from the Hub and prints a one-sentence answer.
